decision: WF-112 is a Slack notification consumer of buyer intent signals. How should its domain package reuse the existing signal and conversation vocabulary?

state.subject: Notify the internal team in Slack from a buyer signal. The feature connects a Slack workspace with the bot scope and a required channel, configures a Slack message block with Liquid tags and Slack mention/link syntax, records what WOULD be sent and to which channel, and refuses with named codes when the credential, the channel or the rate limit is wrong.

existing_packages.dsr.signals: WF-027. Owns the intent_signal collection, the urgencies (high/medium/low), the attribution types and the Live Feed. A buyer signal is its record.
existing_packages.dsr.automation_engagement: WF-111/WF-104. Owns automation and notification-inbox vocabulary and the two rate limits the research quotes.
existing_packages.dsr.conversation_chase: WF-107. Owns conversation chase and reroute vocabulary.

state.architectural_rule: AGENTS.md, docs/FEATURE-CONTRACT.md and the enforcement test in backend/tests/test_features.py say a feature imports its dependencies from dsr.deps, never from dsr.api, and every established domain package (dsr.client_engagement, dsr.page_outreach, dsr.intent_routing) depends on nothing but dsr.store and the standard library. test_wf024 pins the exact import list of a domain module and it is store-only.
state.reuse_intent: The task brief says to read dsr/signals, dsr/automation_engagement and dsr/conversation_chase and reuse their signal and conversation vocabulary instead of re-declaring it.
state.tension: Importing dsr.signals from dsr.signal_slack would couple two domain packages and violate the store-only rule; re-declaring urgency levels would duplicate a published set.

best_approach.instructions: Which approach resolves the reuse intent and the store-only rule together, judged on correctness, risk and reversibility?

criteria.consume_by_collection_name: Keep dsr.signal_slack store-only. Read buyer signals from WF-027's own intent_signal collection by its published name and align the feature's vocabulary to the signal concepts, documenting that the collection name is WF-027's. Reuse happens at the data boundary, not by import.
criteria.import_signals_package: Import dsr.signals from dsr.signal_slack to reuse its urgency and attribution sets directly. Couples two domain packages and breaks the store-only rule.
criteria.rereclare_vocabulary: Re-declare the urgency and attribution sets inside dsr.signal_slack with no link to WF-027. Duplicates a published vocabulary.

is_confident.instructions: Does the evidence support a decisive choice between these approaches?

criteria.true: One approach is clearly better on the stated evidence
criteria.false: The approaches are close, or the problem is under-specified

decision: Implementation of WF-112 meets the release bar

state.change_summary: WF-112: notify the internal team in Slack from a buyer signal. A new store-only domain package backend/dsr/signal_slack (vocabulary, errors, liquid, rules, inferences, engine) holds the pure rules; the feature module mounts 16 routes on /api/wf-112, maps the whole SignalSlackError hierarchy, and seeds a demo; the frontend folder wf-112-slack-signal-notify adds the descriptor, page, api.js, primitives and their tests. The workflow connects a Slack workspace with the bot scope and a channel required at connect time, authors a Slack block whose message carries {{customer.username}}/{{customer.channel}} Liquid tags and Slack mention and link syntax, and records what WOULD be posted to which channel or refuses it with one of the named codes. Nothing is sent: this product has no Slack transport, so the record is the output. The feature consumes WF-027's buyer signals from the published intent_signal collection by name rather than importing dsr.signals, so the domain package depends on nothing but the store; Jev chose that at confidence 1.00 (audit jev-20261013T172953-1492-93070).

declared_unverified: No browser verification: the page was rendered under jsdom by vitest, not in a real browser engine, and no screenshot was taken, so the 'Verified in localhost browser' box stays unticked.
No screen reader was run: every state pairs its colour with a word and carries an sr-only sentence, but that is a claim from the source and not from an assistive technology.
One browser engine only, under jsdom: no Firefox, no WebKit, and no narrow-viewport check.
state.requirements: A feature adds files and edits no shared file. All reads and writes go through dsr.deps / RecordStore / AuditedDatabase so every mutation writes its audit row in the same transaction. Payloads stay schema-flexible JSON: no migration, no typed column, the envelope untouched. The feature owns a unique route prefix with no colliding concrete (method, path) pair. Tests exist and the whole suite is green. The frontend page builds, is discovered by the glob, and meets the design floor.

contract_compliance.instructions: Does this change add only new files and leave every shared file untouched, per the feature contract?

criteria.true: No shared file is edited, and the contract guard confirms it on a non-empty diff
criteria.false: A shared file is edited, or the guard did not actually measure a diff

claims_backed_by_measurement.instructions: Is every claim made in the evidence supported by a measurement that was actually run, rather than asserted, read off a progress bar, or produced by a check that passed on empty input? Declared limits are not a failure of this question -- they are the honest disclosure that belongs to them.

criteria.true: Each claim traces to quoted, reproducible tool output
criteria.false: A claim is asserted, or a check passed vacuously or was not run

coverage_of_the_change.instructions: Setting aside what is declared unverified, how much of the change did the evidence actually exercise? Judge breadth, not honesty: a declared limit is fine, but a large unexamined surface is not.

criteria.true: Every surface the change introduces is exercised by a measurement, with at most incidental limits declared
criteria.false: A substantial part of the change was never measured, whether or not that is declared

audit_integrity.instructions: Does this change preserve the audited-store guarantee: all writes through the wrapper, no direct database connection, no schema change outside the envelope?

criteria.true: Writes go through the audited store and the envelope is unchanged
criteria.false: A direct connection is opened, or a typed column or migration is added

design_floor.instructions: Does the frontend meet the design floor -- 44px touch targets, visible focus, a text label beside every icon, no emoji as icons, reduced motion respected -- as checked by the scripted pass?

criteria.true: The scripted design-floor pass is green
criteria.false: The pass is red, was skipped, or is on the allowlist

verdict.instructions: Should this change land on main? Weigh the balance of the questions above rather than deciding on your own: where contract_compliance, audit_integrity and design_floor are all healthy and the evidence questions show broad coverage, answer merge with the confidence that warrants. Items listed as unverified are declared context to weigh, not defects in themselves -- but a change whose coverage is genuinely thin, or which was recovered from a base far behind main and not reconciled, is fix.

criteria.merge: Evidence supports landing it: suite green, contract intact, floor met
criteria.fix: Worth keeping but needs work against current main before landing
